title: Docs: SIEM-ready audit export (beta) — overview + Splunk/Datadog setup + dedupe guidance
author: Elliot Price
description:
Customer documentation draft for SIEM-ready audit export (beta). This PR adds a customer-facing overview + setup guides for Splunk HEC and Datadog Logs intake, plus explicit delivery semantics and deduplication guidance for at-least-once delivery.

Goals: (1) make beta onboarding self-serve for common SIEM paths (Splunk + Datadog), (2) set correct expectations about duplicates / ordering / retries, (3) document required permissions, encryption posture, and what data is included/excluded (PII redaction rules), (4) include troubleshooting and recommended queries/dashboards.

Non-goals: final GA copy, additional sinks beyond Splunk/Datadog/S3, and deep vendor-specific field mappings.

Key content included: overview (what gets exported, supported destinations, limitations), how filtering works (include/exclude by event type/actor/workspace/environment/time window; safe defaults), delivery guarantees (at-least-once, durable buffering, retries/backoff, DLQ behavior as surfaced in Console), and dedupe guidance (recommended key = event_id; guidance for Splunk and Datadog pipelines; notes for downstream correlation).

Notes: copy intentionally calls out that duplicates are expected under retry/replay and that customers should dedupe by `event.id` (or `event_id`) and optionally `(event.id, schema.version)` depending on their pipeline. Also clarifies that order is best-effort only and may not be strictly increasing across partitions.

Screenshots: omitted (Console UX still behind feature flag; will add once DES-611/613 copy stabilizes).

changed_files: sidebars.js (add Audit Export section under Security)
notable_snippets: Delivery semantics excerpt: "Audit export is at-least-once. Under retries, failover, or replay, the same audit event may be delivered more than once. Consumers must deduplicate."
Dedupe guidance excerpt: "Use `event.id` as the primary dedupe key. If your pipeline transforms events, ensure the original `event.id` is preserved as an immutable field."
Splunk HEC note: "If you enable HEC acknowledgements (recommended), Redwood will treat an event batch as delivered only after ACK is observed; retries may still occur on timeouts."
Datadog note: "HTTP 202 indicates acceptance, not indexing. During 429s, Redwood backs off and retries; duplicates can occur if the intake accepted data but the response was lost."
